items.summary:
▲ Anthropic just released Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2, an upgrade that beats Opus 5.5 on most of its own benchmarks at a lower price.

The key idea is 1 model with 2 safeguard levels. Fable 5.2 runs classifiers that block high-risk cyber and research-biology requests, then hands those to Opus 4.8 or Opus 5. Mythos 5.2 is the same model without those blocks, for vetted orgs only.

On FrontierCode 2.0, Fable 5.2 scores 49.1% at Xhigh effort, vs 45.5% for Opus 5.5 and 42.8% for GPT-6 Astra. At High effort it matches Opus 5.5's best score for roughly half the cost per task. It is a trade-off though: Gemini 4 Carbon still leads AutomationBench (53.9% vs 51.4%), and every score is self-reported.

Pricing is $8 / $40 per million tokens, with a 1M-token context window and 128K output. Fast mode runs up to 2.5x faster at $16 / $80. API ID: claude-fable-5-2......

items.title: Meta’s AI age-check goes global: Can it protect teens? | Mental Health News | Al Jazeera
items.summary:
Meta has rolled out artificial intelligence (AI)-powered age-estimation technology worldwide in an effort to better detect teenage users who signed up for its social media platforms with an adult’s birth date.

The world’s largest social media company announced the change on Monday, saying that millions more young people worldwide would be placed in its Teen Accounts following the implementation of the new technology amid concerns that its platforms have failed to protect teenagers. [...] The AI searches a user’s account to find “contextual clues” that point to their age. Examples given by Meta include “birthday celebrations or mentions of school grades”.

It also uses “visual cues” in pictures and videos on the account, but Meta says that this does not extend to facial recognition. [...] Meta, which owns Instagram, Facebook, WhatsApp and Threads, said on Monday that it had started using its AI age-estimation system on Instagram accounts around the world.

“Since first introducing this technology, we’ve been placing more teens in age-appropriate protections and are encouraged by the results. Based on that success, today we’re expanding this technology globally,” the company said.

items.title: He’s using AI to screen existing compounds for therapeutic potential | University of Pittsburgh
items.summary: Developing pharmaceuticals using AI isn’t new, but it is laborious and often leads to a dead end. “If you generate a brand-new molecule, that’s actually a limitation,” Wang said. “A lot of compounds can’t be synthesized, and that is a big issue.” [...] This back and forth is the GAN’s training. Over time, the generator learns to generate fingerprints that more closely resemble those of real molecules. Researchers then search chemical databases for existing compounds with similar footprints; the AI-generated pattern leads to the discovery of real molecules that researchers can test — no need to synthesize a new molecule. [...] In a paper published Oct. 28 in the journal Science Advances, Wang outlined Full-Spectrum Generative Lead Discovery (FSGLD), a novel, practical and reusable framework that takes advantage of generative AI to screen for existing compounds with potential for therapeutic development.

results.input: Bạn là gì và làm được những gì?

result.actual_text:
Tôi là một trợ lý nghiên cứu được thiết kế để hỗ trợ việc tìm kiếm, trích xuất và định dạng thông tin từ nhiều nguồn khác nhau. Tôi có thể thực hiện các nhiệm vụ sau:

1. **Tìm kiếm trên mạng xã hội (Twitter/X)**:
   - Lấy các bài đăng (tweet) mới nhất hoặc nổi bật từ một tài khoản cụ thể (ví dụ: Elon Musk, Sam Altman).
   - Tìm kiếm các bài đăng theo chủ đề (ví dụ: "AI", "GPT-5").

2. **Tìm kiếm tin tức và thông tin trên web**:
   - Tìm kiếm tin tức thời sự hoặc thông tin chung trên internet.
   - Chỉ định rõ chủ đề (ví dụ: "AI", "máy học") và khoảng thời gian (ví dụ: "hôm nay", "tuần này").

3. **Đọc nội dung từ một URL cụ thể**:
   - Truy cập và trích xuất nội dung từ một trang web hoặc bài viết (ví dụ: một bài báo, trang blog).

4. **Tìm kiếm bài báo khoa học trên arXiv**:
   - Tìm các bài báo khoa học theo chủ đề (ví dụ: "deep learning", "neural networks").
   - Đọc nội dung chi tiết của một bài báo cụ thể nếu có mã arXiv.

5. **Tìm kiếm kho mã nguồn mở trên GitHub**:
   - Tìm các dự án mã nguồn mở theo từ khóa, ngôn ngữ lập trình (ví dụ: Python, JavaScript) và tiêu chí sắp xếp (sao, fork, cập nhật).

6. **Định dạng và trình bày thông tin**:
   - Trình bày dữ liệu đã thu thập theo các mẫu chuẩn (ví dụ: tóm tắt ngắn, danh sách phân mục, bài báo chi tiết).

7. **Xác nhận trước khi thực hiện hành động**:
   - Nếu cần đăng nội dung lên Telegram, tôi sẽ yêu cầu xác nhận trước để đảm bảo người dùng đồng ý.

8. **Tra cứu chính sách nội bộ**:
   - Tra cứu các quy định về dữ liệu, công cụ sử dụng, hoặc nghiên cứu AI.

Tôi không thể thực hiện các nhiệm vụ như giải toán, viết mã nguồn tổng quát hoặc xử lý các yêu cầu không liên quan đến dữ liệu hoặc thông tin. Nếu bạn cần hỗ trợ, vui lòng cung cấp chi tiết yêu cầu (ví dụ: tìm bài đăng của Elon Musk về AI, hoặc đọc nội dung từ một trang web cụ thể). Tôi sẽ giúp bạn một cách chính xác và hiệu quả!

items.title: Meta’s AI age-check goes global: Can it protect teens? | Mental Health News | Al Jazeera
items.summary:
Meta has rolled out artificial intelligence (AI)-powered age-estimation technology worldwide in an effort to better detect teenage users who signed up for its social media platforms with an adult’s birth date.

The world’s largest social media company announced the change on Monday, saying that millions more young people worldwide would be placed in its Teen Accounts following the implementation of the new technology amid concerns that its platforms have failed to protect teenagers. [...] The AI searches a user’s account to find “contextual clues” that point to their age. Examples given by Meta include “birthday celebrations or mentions of school grades”.

It also uses “visual cues” in pictures and videos on the account, but Meta says that this does not extend to facial recognition. [...] Meta, which owns Instagram, Facebook, WhatsApp and Threads, said on Monday that it had started using its AI age-estimation system on Instagram accounts around the world.

“Since first introducing this technology, we’ve been placing more teens in age-appropriate protections and are encouraged by the results. Based on that success, today we’re expanding this technology globally,” the company said.

Over time, the generator learns to generate fingerprints that more closely resemble those of real molecules. Researchers then search chemical databases for existing compounds with similar footprints; the AI-generated pattern leads to the discovery of real molecules that researchers can test — no need to synthesize a new molecule. [...] In a paper published Oct. 28 in the journal Science Advances, Wang outlined Full-Spectrum Generative Lead Discovery (FSGLD), a novel, practical and reusable framework that takes advantage of generative AI to screen for existing compounds with potential for therapeutic development.

items.title: Recent Advances in AI Are Creating a ‘Paradigm Shift’ for Robotics | Research UC Berkeley
items.summary:
In recent months, artificial intelligence agents that can reason, plan and use external tools to accomplish multistep tasks have already reshaped computer coding, online shopping, dinner reservations and cyberattacks.

Robotics might be next.

Ken Goldberg, a UC Berkeley roboticist and professor of engineering, said new models make it possible for teams of AI agents to develop robot-control programs, test them in simulated environments and revise the code when something doesn’t work. [...] Traditionally, engineers can directly program the software that tells robots how to perceive objects, plan movements and control their actions, a process called model-based robotics. Or, with model-free robotics, they can train robots to learn behaviors from demonstrations through imitation learning. The first approach requires extensive engineering, while the second needs enormous amounts of data and time. [...] Berkeley-based Ambi Robotics, which specializes in logistics and warehouse order fulfillment, applied the new methods earlier this year to analyze parcel sorting data and test updates to robot behavior. Tests showed an increased capacity of over 15,000 packages sorted annually per robot; the change is now deployed across 30% of the company’s U.S. fleet.

items.title: Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20
items.summary:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

A vocal section of the American electorate were seeking assurances that AI companies will not overload power grids, while many candidates ran on a ticket of holding hyperscalers to account.

Before a single vote was counted, though, OpenAI, the company behind ChatGPT, had unveiled its ‘Grid Protectors Program’ – an initiative that will see its future computing campuses ease pressure on the grid. [...] “Data centres are paying more so families and small businesses can pay less, and our goal with every contract we sign under this framework is to deliver value for them,” she says

At OpenAI, the bigger picture is always in focus.

“With US data centre capacity projected to exceed 100 gigawatts by 2030⁠, we have a once-in-a-generation opportunity to strengthen the electric grid by building campuses that can adjust their power use when communities need it most,” the company says. [...] OpenAI is working to ensure its data centres can actually benefit grids, rather than overloading them. Credit: Anna Moneymaker/Getty

## What is OpenAI’s Grid Protectors Program?

The programme, which was announced on 2 November, commits the company to working with utilities, regulators and policymakers on arrangements for cutting the power use of its data centres at times of need.

items.title: OpenAI wants to be Google - Fast Company
items.summary:
OpenAI needs to build analytics that show advertisers the consumer intent based on their prompts. I want to know which categories of intent my impressions ran against. I want to know whether those people were exploring, comparing, or ready to act, and which needs and product criteria drove that engagement. I want to know which kinds of sweater prompts turned into business and, just as important, which didn’t. Google’s advertisers have had some version of that map for two decades. It’s why [...] |

That comparison is where every sweater brand wants to be standing, and OpenAI has started selling the spot. Advertisers can buy on a CPM or CPC basis through OpenAI’s beta self-service Ads Manager, measure conversions with a pixel and Conversions API, and access campaign-level performance reporting. OpenAI is also testing Sponsored Agents, which let a user start a separate conversation with an advertiser after clicking an ad.

So the plumbing exists.

## A SEARCH-CALIBER AD PLATFORM [...] OpenAI already has the hard part down, the thing Google spent years teaching people to do. People are telling ChatGPT their goals, problems, preferences, objections, and purchase criteria in their own words. What it hasn’t built is the advertiser’s map of all that intent.

items.title: Anthropic and OpenAI are coming for the development workflow | InfoWorld
items.summary: This is clearly where the frontier labs are moving, even though they’ve all benefited from an industry that provided neutral spaces to build. For example, OpenAI developed Pando, a Git back end for its own monorepo, to handle more engineers and agents reading and writing code concurrently. Its engineers kept using Git. OpenAI retained compatibility with the protocol and client and contributed improvements upstream. That compatibility let it rebuild the back end around the way its engineers [...] This pressure to maximize profitability helps explain why frontier labs like Anthropic and OpenAI are aggressively adding functionality to own more of the developer’s workflow. On November 4, OpenAI announced an agreement to buy Pierre, the company behind Code Storage and the open source libraries Codex already uses to browse files and review changes. OpenAI wants Codex to be where developers work, from the first branch an agent creates through deployment of the application. There’s money in [...] OpenAI or Anthropic could build the place developers prefer to work. The question is what happens when a team likes that place and wants a rival’s agent for a particular job. Maybe a startup has built a tool that can track down the intermittent test failure that’s had the team stumped for a week. Give it access to the code and test history the team has authorized, and it gets a chance to prove itself. Ask the team to move its work to a new platform first, and it probably never gets to try.
